claims.text: A minor reactive dopant addition to CoCrFeNi will promote in situ formation of an oxide layer during sliding.
The dopant-induced oxide layer will be continuous and lubricious.
The oxide layer forms through dopant segregation to the sliding interface followed by oxidation.
Under sliding and elevated-temperature conditions, the reactive dopant will oxidize preferentially.
Preferential dopant oxidation will produce a low-shear-strength oxide film.
The low-shear-strength oxide film will reduce adhesive interactions at the sliding contact.
Reduced adhesive interactions will lower friction and wear.
The doped alloy will have statistically significantly lower coefficients of friction than undoped CoCrFeNi throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The doped alloy will have statistically significantly lower wear rates than undoped CoCrFeNi throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
Undoped CoCrFeNi exhibits higher friction under comparable sliding conditions than the proposed doped alloy.
Undoped CoCrFeNi exhibits greater wear under comparable sliding conditions than the proposed doped alloy.
The proposed improvement is expected only in an oxidizing environment between room temperature and 800 °C under moderate-to-high sliding loads.
Conditions outside the stated temperature, load, or oxidizing-environment boundaries may not produce the self-lubricating oxide.
